title: Payment processing microservice
blurb: Internet-facing payment API, card data store, and external gateway. Classic product-security whiteboard.

project.name: Payment Processing System
project.description: Secure payment processing microservice for a multi-tenant SaaS checkout.

threats.name: Payment amount tampering
threats.description: Attacker modifies payment amount in the client or a replayed request.

threats.name: Payment data theft
threats.description: Attacker steals cardholder data from the API, logs, or database.

threats.name: Gateway credential abuse
threats.description: Stolen gateway credentials let an attacker charge or refund without authorization.

mitigations.name: Server-side amount validation
mitigations.description: Recompute payable amount from authoritative cart/pricing; never trust client totals.

mitigations.name: Encryption and tokenization
mitigations.description: TLS in transit; tokenize PAN; encrypt residual sensitive fields at rest with KMS.

mitigations.name: Short-lived secrets and least privilege
mitigations.description: Store gateway credentials in a secrets manager; rotate; scope keys; audit gateway calls.

prompts.title: Walk the trust boundaries in this model. Which crossings matter most and why?
prompts.answerMarkdown: Name the zones: Internet, Application VPC, Data plane, External gateway. Highest-risk crossings are browser → Payment API (untrusted input, card data in flight) and API → gateway (credentials + card data leave your boundary). Persist to DB is still sensitive but usually inside stronger controls. Interview move: pick one crossing, name the asset on the wire, and say the control that must sit on that edge.

prompts.title: How would you mitigate payment amount tampering end to end?
prompts.answerMarkdown: Never trust client totals. Reprice server-side from cart/SKU rules, bind the payable amount to a signed server order id, and verify the gateway authorization amount matches that order. Log mismatches. Add idempotency keys so replays cannot double-charge. Mention integrity of webhooks from the gateway as a follow-up.

prompts.title: What would you say about PCI scope reduction for this architecture?
prompts.answerMarkdown: Prefer tokenization / hosted fields so PAN never hits your app or DB. If you must touch card data, isolate the payment service, encrypt at rest with KMS, minimize logs, and network-segment the data plane. Map assets: cardholder data vs transaction metadata. State residual risk and who owns the compensating control.
